Ahmed Sobhan with Fazlul Karim---------For Appellant.
Shaukat Ali Khan, A. Baset Mazumdar, Aftabuddin Ahmed and Afsaruddin Ahmed Khan -------For Respondent.
full_judgment: 6. In considering an application under Order 38 Rule 5, the learned Subordinate Judge is required to be satisfied about the intention of the defendants, who must not act in a manner with the properties to obstruct delay or defeat an execution of a possible decree. Such satisfaction must be derived from the record which must reveal that the defendant is either about to dispose of the whole or part of the property or is about to remove any part of the properly from the local limit of the jurisdiction of the court. The learned Subordinate Judge in the instant case has found that the defendant was a man of means and he had the capacity to pay decretal dues. The learned Subordinate Judge ought to have considered that it is not the present capacity of the defendant to pay for which an application is made. An application is always made to ensure the possibility of a future payment and as such the learned Subordinate Judge should have directed himself to consider the allegation: made in the application filed by the respondent under Order 38 Rule 5. Present resourcefulness of the defendant is not the criterion for refusing a prayer under Order 38 Rule 5. Furthermore the resourcefulness of the defendant is accepted by the learned subordinate Judge order on the basis of what have been stated in sub-paragraph (7) of the written objection. The names of different organisations have been given of which neither any address nor proof of their financial soundness have been given. From these names only it will be too much to presume the capacity of the defendant to satisfy a possible decree.
